title: Pure template expansion with atomic apply
description:
Split template instantiation into a pure expansion function that produces a graph delta and an executor that applies the delta atomically under one repository lock. Validate transform kinds at registry load.

## Background

`apply_template_with` (`commands/template.rs:211-448`) interleaves validation and writes. The pre-mutation checks (`prevalidate_node_writes`, `prevalidate_acyclic`) shrink the failure window, but nothing holds a lock across the apply: a mid-sequence I/O failure or a concurrent mutation between the `list_issues()` snapshot and the writes leaves partially-created nodes and edges persisted. Additionally, a template with an unknown transform kind loads cleanly and only fails at apply (`template.rs:316-323`), though this is a static config error the loader should catch alongside its other structural checks (`templates.rs:708-822`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-1: A pure function expands (template, container snapshot, anchor bindings) into an explicit graph delta (issues to create, edges to add, edges to remove) with no storage access.
- [hard] REQ-2: Apply executes the delta under a single repository lock; a validation or write failure leaves the issue store observably unchanged, verified by a test that injects a write failure mid-apply.
- [hard] REQ-3: A template declaring an unknown transform kind fails registry load with an error naming the template and kind; apply never sees it.
- [hard] REQ-4: Existing apply behavior (plan-bracket scaffold, idempotent re-apply, forced refresh) is preserved by the existing integration suite.

## Notes

All-or-nothing may be implemented by compensation (rolling back created artifacts on failure) rather than a journal, as long as the observable outcome holds under the injected-failure test. Edge writes must still produce the same events and transitive-reduction behavior as the standard dependency path.
